en bachelor.explanation: "En bachelor" means "a bachelor's degree". To say you are studying for one, use "at læse" (to study): "Hun læser en bachelor i historie" (She is studying for a bachelor's degree in history). To say an unmarried man, use "en ungkarl" (an unmarried man): "Min onkel er ungkarl" (My uncle is an unmarried man).

en backup.explanation: "En backup" means "a backup". To say you get your files back, use "at gendanne" (to restore) with "fra" (from): "Jeg gendanner mine filer fra en backup" (I restore my files from a backup).

en badedragt.explanation: "En badedragt" means "a swimsuit". It is built from "at bade" (to bathe) and "en dragt" (a suit). To say you put it on, use "at tage på" (to put on): "Jeg tager badedragten på" (I put on my swimsuit).

en bademåtte.explanation: "En bademåtte" means "a bath mat". It is built from "at bade" (to bathe) and "en måtte" (a mat). The part "måtte" (mat) is also in "en gulvmåtte" (a floor mat).

en badestrand.explanation: "En badestrand" means "a bathing beach". It is built from "at bade" (to bathe) and "en strand" (a beach). To say you swim in the sea, use "at bade" (to swim): "Vi bader i havet hele sommeren" (We swim in the sea all summer).

en badevægt.explanation: "En badevægt" means "a bathroom scale". It is built from "at bade" (to bathe) and "en vægt" (a weight). To say you step on it, use "at stå på" (to stand on): "Jeg står på badevægten hver morgen" (I step on the bathroom scale every morning).

en bagagebærer.explanation: "En bagagebærer" means "a luggage rack / bike rack". It is built from "en bagage" (luggage) and "at bære" (to carry). To say you fasten a bag to the back of a bike, use "at spænde fast" (to strap on): "Jeg spænder tasken fast på bagagebæreren" (I strap the bag onto the rack).

en bageplade.explanation: "En bageplade" means "a baking tray". It is built from "at bage" (to bake) and "en plade" (a sheet). To say you cover it so nothing sticks, use "bagepapir" (baking paper): "Læg bagepapir på bagepladen" (Put baking paper on the baking tray).

en bager.explanation: "En bager" means "a baker". It comes from "at bage" (to bake). To say you go to the bakery, Danish names the person instead of the shop: "Jeg går til bageren" (I am going to the bakery), literally "I am going to the baker".

en baggrund.explanation: "En baggrund" means "a background". To say what is behind the main part of a picture or a scene, use "i baggrunden" (in the background): "Man kan se bjerge i baggrunden" (You can see mountains in the background). To talk about a person's past, such as their education and life so far, it also means "background": "Hun har en anden baggrund" (She has a different background).

en baggård.explanation: "En baggård" means "a backyard". It is built from "bag" (behind) and "en gård" (a yard). To talk about a farm, the same word "gård" is used: "Han bor på en gård" (He lives on a farm).

en baglygte.explanation: "En baglygte" means "a taillight". It is built from "bag" (back) and "en lygte" (a light). To tell someone to switch it on, use "at tænde" (to switch on): "Husk at tænde baglygten på cyklen" (Remember to switch on the taillight on the bike).

en bagning.explanation: "En bagning" means "a baking". It comes from "at bage" (to bake). The ending "-ning" turns a verb into a noun in many words, such as "en tegning" (a drawing) from "at tegne" (to draw).

en bagside.explanation: "En bagside" means "a back / downside". When you point to the rear of a page, a card or an envelope, it means "back": "Bagsiden af kuverten er tom" (The back of the envelope is empty). When you talk about the unwelcome part of something good, it means "downside": "Det er medaljens bagside" (That is the flip side of the medal).

en baguette.explanation: "En baguette" means "a baguette". To say what is in it, use "med" (with): "en baguette med ost" (a baguette with cheese).

en bakke.explanation: "En bakke" means "a hill". When you carry cups or plates on a flat board with a rim, it also means "a tray": "Jeg bærer en bakke med kaffe" (I carry a tray with coffee).

en bakterie.explanation: "En bakterie" means "a bacterium". Spell it with a "k", not a "c" as in English. To say soap kills germs, use "at dræbe" (to kill): "Sæbe dræber bakterier" (Soap kills bacteria).

en balje.explanation: "En balje" means "a tub". To talk about the tub you wash dishes in, add "opvaske" (washing-up): "Jeg skyller glassene i opvaskebaljen" (I rinse the glasses in the washing-up bowl).

en balkon.explanation: "En balkon" means "a balcony". To say where you are sitting, use "på" (on): "Jeg sidder på balkonen" (I am sitting on the balcony).

en ballet.explanation: "En ballet" means "a ballet". To say someone does ballet as a dancer, use "at danse ballet" (to dance ballet) without "en": "Hun danser ballet" (She dances ballet).

en ballon.explanation: "En ballon" means "a balloon". To say you fill a balloon with air, use "at puste op" (to blow up): "Jeg puster ballonen op" (I blow up the balloon).

en bamse.explanation: "En bamse" means "a teddy bear". When you describe a big, gentle, cuddly person, it also means "a teddy bear": "Han er en rigtig bamse" (He is a real teddy bear).

en banan.explanation: "En banan" means "a banana". To say you take the skin off, use "at skrælle" (to peel): "Jeg skræller en banan" (I peel a banana).

en bandage.explanation: "En bandage" means "a bandage". For a small sticky one on a cut, use "et plaster" (an adhesive bandage): "Jeg sætter et plaster på fingeren" (I put an adhesive bandage on my finger).

en bande.explanation: "En bande" means "a gang". When you talk about a group of friends, it also means "gang": "Hele banden kommer" (The whole gang is coming).

en bane.explanation: "En bane" means "a court", as in a sports court. When you talk about the path that runners run along or trains travel on, it also means "a track": "Løberne står klar på banen" (The runners are ready on the track).

en banegård.explanation: "En banegård" means "a railway station". It is built from "en bane" (a railway line) and "en gård" (a yard). To name the main station of a Danish city, "hoved" (main) goes in front: "Københavns Hovedbanegård" (Copenhagen Central Station).

en bank.explanation: "En bank" means "a bank", as in the place for money. To say you are going to the bank, use "i" (in): "Jeg går i banken i dag" (I am going to the bank today).

en bankkonto.explanation: "En bankkonto" means "a bank account". It is built from "en bank" (a bank) and "en konto" (an account). To say you open one, use "at oprette" (to set up): "Jeg vil gerne oprette en bankkonto" (I would like to open a bank account).

en bankrådgiver.explanation: "En bankrådgiver" means "a bank adviser". It is built from "en bank" (a bank) and "en rådgiver" (an adviser). To say you are meeting one, use "et møde med" (a meeting with): "Jeg har et møde med min bankrådgiver" (I have a meeting with my bank adviser).

en barbermaskine.explanation: "En barbermaskine" means "an electric shaver". It is built from "at barbere" (to shave) and "en maskine" (a machine). For a razor you use by hand, say "en barberhøvl" (a razor): "Jeg køber en ny barberhøvl" (I am buying a new razor).

en barista.explanation: "En barista" means "a barista". Do not mix it up with "en bartender" (a bartender). To talk about the person who makes coffee, say: "Baristaen laver en cappuccino" (The barista makes a cappuccino). To talk about the person who makes mixed drinks, say: "Bartenderen laver en cocktail" (The bartender makes a cocktail).

en barndom.explanation: "En barndom" means "a childhood". To say something happened when you were young, use "i" (in) before "min barndom" (my childhood): "I min barndom boede vi på landet" (In my childhood we lived in the country).

en barndomsven.explanation: "En barndomsven" means "a childhood friend". It is built from "en barndom" (a childhood) and "en ven" (a friend). To talk about a woman or girl, use "en barndomsveninde" (a female childhood friend): "Hun er min barndomsveninde" (She is my childhood friend).

en barnedåb.explanation: "En barnedåb" means "a christening". It is built from "et barn" (a child) and "en dåb" (a baptism). To say a baby is christened, use "at døbe" (to baptize): "Vi skal døbe babyen i kirken i morgen" (We are going to christen the baby in the church tomorrow).

en barnepige.explanation: "En barnepige" means "a nanny / babysitter". It is built from "et barn" (a child) and "en pige" (a girl). To say you are the babysitter for someone, use "at være barnepige for" (to be a babysitter for): "Jeg er barnepige for min niece" (I am the babysitter for my niece).

en barnevogn.explanation: "En barnevogn" means "a baby carriage". To say you take the baby for a walk, use "at gå en tur med" (to go for a walk with): "Jeg går en tur med barnevognen" (I am going for a walk with the baby carriage).

en bartender.explanation: "En bartender" means "a bartender". Another word for the same job is "en barmand" (a barman): "Barmanden smiler til gæsterne" (The barman smiles at the guests).

en base.explanation: "En base" means "a base", as in a military base. In chemistry, it means a substance that reacts with an acid: "En base kan neutralisere en syre" (A base can neutralize an acid). For the bottom of an object, use "en bund" (a bottom): "Der er vand i bunden af flasken" (There is water in the bottom of the bottle).

en bedrager.explanation: "En bedrager" means "a con artist". It comes from "at bedrage" (to deceive). To talk about the crime, use "bedrageri" (fraud): "Han blev dømt for bedrageri" (He was convicted of fraud).

en bedrift.explanation: "En bedrift" means "an achievement / feat". To say someone did something impressive, say: "Hans bedrift blev fejret af hele landet" (His achievement was celebrated by the whole country). When you talk about a business, it also means "business", as in "en landbrugsbedrift" (a farm business).

en bedstefar.explanation: "En bedstefar" means "a grandfather". To say he is your mother's father, use "morfar": "Min morfar er pensionist" (My mother's father is retired). To say he is your father's father, use "farfar": "Min farfar bor i Odense" (My father's father lives in Odense).

en bedstemor.explanation: "En bedstemor" means "a grandmother". To say she is your mother's mother, use "mormor": "Min mormor bager boller" (My mother's mother bakes buns). To say she is your father's mother, use "farmor": "Min farmor bor i Odense" (My father's mother lives in Odense).

en bedømmelse.explanation: "En bedømmelse" means "an assessment". It comes from "at bedømme" (to judge). To say you receive one, use "at få" (to get): "Jeg fik en god bedømmelse" (I got a good assessment).

en bedøvelse.explanation: "En bedøvelse" means "an anesthetic". To say someone is under general anesthesia for surgery, use "narkose" (general anesthesia) with "i" (in): "Hun er i narkose" (She is under general anesthesia).

en befolkning.explanation: "En befolkning" means "a population". To say the number of people is rising, use "at vokse" (to grow): "Befolkningen vokser hvert år" (The population grows every year). To talk about one person living in a town, use "en indbygger" (an inhabitant): "Byen har 50.000 indbyggere" (The town has 50,000 inhabitants).

en befrielse.explanation: "En befrielse" means "a liberation". In Denmark, "Befrielsen" (the Liberation) is the name for the end of the German occupation in May 1945. When you feel a burden is gone, it also means "relief": "Det var en befrielse at aflevere opgaven" (It was a relief to hand in the assignment).

en begavelse.explanation: "En begavelse" means "a talent". It comes from "begavet" (gifted). To say someone has great talent, use "stor" (great): "Hun har en stor begavelse" (She has a great talent).

en begivenhed.explanation: "En begivenhed" means "an event". To say an event takes place, use "at finde sted" (to take place): "Begivenheden finder sted i morgen" (The event takes place tomorrow).

en begravelse.explanation: "En begravelse" means "a funeral". To say you attend one, use "at deltage i" (to take part in): "Vi deltager i begravelsen" (We are attending the funeral).

en begrundelse.explanation: "En begrundelse" means "a justification". It is built on "en grund" (a reason). To ask for the reason behind something, say: "Hvad er begrundelsen?" (What is the reason?)

en begrænsning.explanation: "En begrænsning" means "a limitation". It is built on "en grænse" (a border or limit). To say there are no limits, use "ingen" (no): "Der er ingen begrænsninger" (There are no limitations).

en begyndelse.explanation: "En begyndelse" means "a beginning". It is built from "at begynde" (to begin). To say it happens in the first part of something, use "i begyndelsen af" (at the beginning of): "I begyndelsen af filmen er der en storm" (At the beginning of the film there is a storm).

en begynder.explanation: "En begynder" means "a beginner". It comes from "at begynde" (to begin). To talk about a class for beginners, use "et begynderhold" (a beginners' class): "Jeg går på et begynderhold" (I am in a beginners' class).

en behandling.explanation: "En behandling" means "a treatment". It comes from "at behandle" (to treat). When you talk about how someone is treated, it also means "treatment": "Han fik dårlig behandling" (He got bad treatment).

en bekendt.explanation: "En bekendt" means "an acquaintance". To say someone is not a close friend, say: "Han er en bekendt, ikke en nær ven" (He is an acquaintance, not a close friend). When a song or a face seems known to you, the adjective "bekendt" means "familiar": "Sangen lyder bekendt" (The song sounds familiar).

en bekendtgørelse.explanation: "En bekendtgørelse" means "an announcement / regulation". It is built from "bekendt" (known) and "at gøre" (to make): it makes something known. In Denmark, a minister issues a "bekendtgørelse" to set out the details of how a law works.

en bekymring.explanation: "En bekymring" means "a worry". To say you worry, use "at bekymre sig" (literally, to worry yourself): "Jeg bekymrer mig" (I worry). To say you are worried about someone, use the adjective "bekymret" (worried): "Hun er bekymret for sin søn" (She is worried about her son).

en belastning.explanation: "En belastning" means "a strain". It comes from "at belaste" (to put a load on). To take the strain off someone, use "at aflaste" (to relieve): "Jeg aflaster dig i dag" (I am relieving you today).

en belønning.explanation: "En belønning" means "a reward". To say what you get as a reward, use "som" (as): "Du får en is som belønning" (You get an ice cream as a reward).

en benzinstation.explanation: "En benzinstation" means "a gas station". It is built from "benzin" (gasoline) and "en station" (a station). To say you fill the car with fuel, use "at tanke" (to fill up): "Jeg skal tanke på benzinstationen" (I need to fill up at the gas station).

en beregning.explanation: "En beregning" means "a calculation". To say you work something out, use "at lave" (to make): "Jeg laver en beregning af prisen" (I am making a calculation of the price). Do not mix it up with "en regning" (a bill): "Jeg betaler regningen" (I pay the bill).

en bersærk.explanation: "En bersærk" means "a berserker". Danish spells it with "æ", where English has "berserk". To say someone loses control in anger, use "at gå bersærk" (to go berserk): "Han gik bersærk i butikken" (He went berserk in the shop).

en berøring.explanation: "En berøring" means "a touch". It comes from "at berøre" (to touch): "Han berørte min arm" (He touched my arm). To describe a gentle one, add "blid" (gentle): "en blid berøring" (a gentle touch).

en besiddelse.explanation: "En besiddelse" means "a possession". To talk about a person's belongings, use the plural: "personlige besiddelser" (personal belongings). When you talk about having something illegal on you, it also means "possession": "besiddelse af stoffer" (possession of drugs).

en besked.explanation: "En besked" means "a message". To ask someone to let you know, use "at give besked" (to let someone know): "Giv mig besked i morgen" (Let me know tomorrow). To say you were told something, use "at få besked" (to get word): "Jeg fik besked om mødet" (I was told about the meeting).

en beskrivelse.explanation: "En beskrivelse" means "a description". It comes from "at beskrive" (to describe). To tell someone to write a short one, use "kort" (short): "Skriv en kort beskrivelse" (Write a short description).

en beskyldning.explanation: "En beskyldning" means "an accusation". It comes from "at beskylde" (to accuse). To say someone makes one, use "at komme med" (to come out with): "Han kom med en beskyldning mod mig" (He made an accusation against me).

en beskæresaks.explanation: "En beskæresaks" means "a pair of pruning shears". It is built from "at beskære" (to prune) and "en saks" (scissors). To say you cut a hedge back, use "at beskære": "Jeg beskærer hækken i april" (I prune the hedge in April).

en beslutning.explanation: "En beslutning" means "a decision". To say you make one, use "at træffe" (to make): "Vi træffer en beslutning" (We make a decision).

en beslutningsproces.explanation: "En beslutningsproces" means "a decision-making process". It is built from "en beslutning" (a decision) and "en proces" (a process). To say people take part, use "med i" (in on): "Medarbejderne er med i beslutningsprocessen" (The employees take part in the decision-making process).

en beslutningstager.explanation: "En beslutningstager" means "a decision-maker". It is built from "en beslutning" (a decision) and "at tage" (to take). To say who has the last word, add "endelig" (final): "Direktøren er den endelige beslutningstager" (The director is the final decision-maker).

en bestemmelse.explanation: "En bestemmelse" means "a provision". It comes from "at bestemme" (to decide). To say what a provision requires, use "ifølge" (according to): "Ifølge bestemmelsen skal du betale i dag" (According to the provision, you must pay today).

en bestilling.explanation: "En bestilling" means "an order", as in an order placed in a shop. It comes from "at bestille" (to order). To ask whether an order has arrived, say: "Har du modtaget min bestilling?" (Have you received my order?)

en bestseller.explanation: "En bestseller" means "a bestseller". To say a book is among the best-selling ones, use "en bestsellerliste" (a bestseller list): "Bogen ligger på bestsellerlisten" (The book is on the bestseller list).

en bestyrelse.explanation: "En bestyrelse" means "a board", as in the group that leads a company or an association. To say you are a member, use "at sidde i" (to sit in): "Hun sidder i bestyrelsen" (She is on the board).

en besætning.explanation: "En besætning" means "a crew", as in the people working on a ship or a plane. On a farm, it also means all the animals kept there: "en kvægbesætning" (a herd of cattle).

en besættelse.explanation: "En besættelse" means "an occupation", as in an army taking over a country (never a job). In Denmark, "besættelsen" (the occupation) is the name for the German occupation from 1940 to 1945. When you cannot stop thinking about something, it also means "obsession": "Det er blevet en besættelse for ham" (It has become an obsession for him).

en besøgende.explanation: "En besøgende" means "a visitor". It comes from "at besøge" (to visit). To say something is for the visitors, use "til" (for): "Der er gratis kaffe til de besøgende" (There is free coffee for the visitors).

en betaling.explanation: "En betaling" means "a payment". To say how you pay, use "med" (by): "betaling med kort" (payment by card).

en betalingsmetode.explanation: "En betalingsmetode" means "a payment method". It is built from "en betaling" (a payment) and "en metode" (a method). In Denmark, "MobilePay" (a Danish phone payment app) is one payment method.

en betingelse.explanation: "En betingelse" means "a condition", as in something that must be true first. For how a person or thing is doing, such as health, use "en tilstand" (a state): "Patientens tilstand er god" (The patient's condition is good).

en betjent.explanation: "En betjent" means "a police officer". A longer word for the same job is "en politibetjent" (a police officer). To say what an officer does on the road, say: "Betjenten standser bilen" (The officer stops the car).

en betragtning.explanation: "En betragtning" means "a consideration". To share your thoughts on a matter, use the plural: "Jeg har nogle betragtninger om sagen" (I have some thoughts on the matter).

en betydning.explanation: "En betydning" means "a meaning". When something matters, it also means "importance": "Det har stor betydning" (It matters a lot).

en betændelse.explanation: "En betændelse" means "an inflammation". When you talk about an infection, it also means "infection": "en betændelse i øret" (an ear infection).

en beundrer.explanation: "En beundrer" means "an admirer". It comes from "at beundre" (to admire). To talk about someone who is secretly in love with you, add "hemmelig" (secret): "en hemmelig beundrer" (a secret admirer).

en bevilling.explanation: "En bevilling" means "a grant", as in money from an authority or a fund. When you talk about an official permit, it also means "permit": "en bevilling til at sælge alkohol" (a permit to sell alcohol).

en bevægelse.explanation: "En bevægelse" means "a movement". To say something is in motion, use "i" (in): "Toget er i bevægelse" (The train is in motion). When you talk about a group working for a cause, it also means "movement": "arbejderbevægelsen" (the labor movement).

en bh.explanation: "En bh" means "a bra". To say you put one on, use "at tage på" (to put on): "Hun tager sin bh på" (She puts on her bra).

en bi.explanation: "En bi" means "a bee". To say a bee stung you, use "at stikke" (to sting): "Jeg blev stukket af en bi" (I was stung by a bee).

en biavler.explanation: "En biavler" means "a beekeeper". It is built from "en bi" (a bee) and "at avle" (to breed). To say someone keeps bees, use "at holde bier" (to keep bees): "Min nabo holder bier" (My neighbor keeps bees).

en bibel.explanation: "En bibel" means "a bible". When you call a book the main guide in a field, it also means "bible": "Bogen er kokkenes bibel" (The book is the chefs' bible).

en bibliotekar.explanation: "En bibliotekar" means "a librarian". The ending "-ar" also makes a word for a person in "en arkivar" (an archivist): "Arkivaren finder gamle papirer" (The archivist finds old papers).

en bidragyder.explanation: "En bidragyder" means "a contributor". It is built from "et bidrag" (a contribution) and "at yde" (to provide). To say someone gives a lot, add "stor" (big): "Firmaet er en stor bidragyder" (The company is a major contributor).

en bikini.explanation: "En bikini" means "a bikini". For a one-piece swimsuit, use "en badedragt" (a swimsuit): "Hun har en badedragt på" (She is wearing a swimsuit).

en bil.explanation: "En bil" means "a car". To say you go by car, use "i bil" (by car), without "en": "Vi kører i bil til Aarhus" (We are going to Aarhus by car).

en bilist.explanation: "En bilist" means "a motorist". It is built from "en bil" (a car) and "-ist". The ending "-ist" makes a word for a person in "en pianist" (a pianist) and "en turist" (a tourist).
